questions.q: In the lab scenario, what is the correct first step for setting up Maria Chen's access?
options: Grant her the admin role immediately so nothing blocks her later
Create her sys_user record with user_name, email, active true, and password_needs_reset checked
Create the Facilities group before she exists as a user
Assign her the itil role before she has a user record
questions.explain: A role or group membership needs a user record to attach to — the sys_user record comes first, per Lesson 1.

questions.q: Why does creating the Facilities group and adding Maria to it not, by itself, give her any permissions?
options: Group membership is about routing and visibility (sys_user_grmember), not about what a user is permitted to do — that's the role's job
Groups automatically grant the itil role to all members
Creating a group always requires admin approval first
Group Email fields block access until configured
questions.explain: This is the group-versus-role distinction from Lessons 2 and 3 applied directly: group membership routes work, roles grant permission.

questions.q: Why is the itil role the right fit for Maria's day-one need to work incidents assigned to her team?
options: itil is the only role that can be assigned to a group
itil maps directly to baseline agent work on tickets, which is exactly what she needs starting Monday
itil automatically grants catalog_admin as well
itil is required before a user record can be created
questions.explain: itil is the baseline agent role for working tickets — matching the actual day-one task, not more and not less.

questions.q: Why does the lab recommend NOT granting catalog_admin to Maria immediately, even though the director mentioned future catalog work?
options: catalog_admin does not exist in ServiceNow
She isn't doing that work yet, and granting access before it's needed violates least privilege for no real benefit
catalog_admin can only be granted to users with the admin role
catalog_admin requires a separate user record
questions.explain: The lab defers catalog_admin until the catalog work actually begins, documenting the future need rather than pre-granting it.

questions.q: Per the lab's final write-up, what should a careful administrator do before finalizing an access decision involving an unfamiliar role like itil?
options: Nothing further — role names are always self-explanatory
Verify what the role contains, confirming it doesn't implicitly grant more than intended, per Lesson 3's containment habit
Immediately upgrade the request to admin to save time later
Skip documentation since the role assignment speaks for itself
questions.explain: The write-up explicitly notes verifying itil 'does not contain anything beyond baseline agent access' — the containment-checking habit from Lesson 3.
